# Zero-Inflated Models

[![CRAN Status
Badge](http://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/ZIM)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ZIM)
[![CRAN Downloads
Total](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/ZIM)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ZIM)

## Overview

Analyze count time series with excess zeros. Two types of statistical
models are supported: Markov regression by Yang et al. (2013)
\<[doi:10.1016/j.stamet.2013.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.stamet.2013.02.001)\>
and state-space models by Yang et al. (2015)
\<[doi:10.1177/1471082X14535530](https://doi.org/10.1177/1471082X14535530)\>.
They are also known as observation-driven and parameter-driven models
respectively in the time series literature. The functions used for
Markov regression or observation-driven models can also be used to fit
ordinary regression models with independent data under the zero-inflated
Poisson (ZIP) or zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) assumption.
Besides, the package contains some miscellaneous functions to compute
density, distribution, quantile, and generate random numbers from ZIP
and ZINB distributions.

## Installation

### Stable Version

Install stable version from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("ZIM")
```

### Development Version

Install development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mingstat/ZIM")
```

## References

- M Yang, GKD Zamba, JE Cavanaugh. Markov regression models for count
  time series with excess zeros: A partial likelihood approach.
  *Statistical Methodology*, 2013, 14:26–38.
  \<[doi:10.1016/j.stamet.2013.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.stamet.2013.02.001)\>

- M Yang, JE Cavanaugh, GKD Zamba. State-space models for count time
  series with excess zeros. *Statistical Modelling*, 2015, 15(1):70–90.
  \<[doi:10.1177/1471082X14535530](https://doi.org/10.1177/1471082X14535530)\>

## All functions

- [`ZIM-package`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/ZIM-package.md)

  Zero-Inflated Models for Count Time Series with Excess Zeros
- [`bshift()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/bshift.md) :
  Backshift Operator Apply the backshift operator or lag operator to a
  time series objective.
- [`dzinb()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dpqr-zinb.md)
  [`pzinb()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dpqr-zinb.md)

  [`rzinb()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dpqr-zinb.md) :
  The Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Distribution
- [`dzip()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dpqr-zip.md)
  [`pzip()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dpqr-zip.md)
  [`qzip()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dpqr-zip.md)
  [`rzip()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dpqr-zip.md) : The
  Zero-Inflated Poisson Distribution
- [`dzim()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dzim.md) : Fitting
  Dynamic Zero-Inflated Models
- [`dzim.control()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dzim.control.md)
  : Auxiliary for Controlling DZIM Fitting
- [`dzim.filter()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dzim.filter.md)
  : Particle Filtering for DZIM
- [`dzim.fit()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dzim.fit.md) :
  Fitter Function for Dynamic Zero-Inflated Models
- [`dzim.plot()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dzim.plot.md)
  : Trace Plots from DZIM
- [`dzim.sim()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dzim.sim.md) :
  Simulate Data from DZIM
- [`dzim.smooth()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/dzim.smooth.md)
  : Particle Smoothing for DZIM
- [`injury`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/injury.md) :
  Example: Injury Series from Occupational Health
- [`pvalue()`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/pvalue.md) :
  Function to Compute P-value.
- [`syph`](https://mingstat.github.io/ZIM/reference/syph.md) : Example:
